newsitem.title: UK: LIFFEE coffee cuts most losses, AAs dominate.
newsitem.headline: LIFFEE coffee cuts most losses, AAs dominate.

text.p: LIFFE coffee futures recovered some ground to end Monday flat to marginally lower after a sharp rebound in New York.
But traders said London's upside was capped by renewed origin selling at the highs.
By the finish, front-month January and nearby March were just $3 off at $1,325 and $1,275 a tonne respectively after ranging within a $30 band.
January was the most active month, accounting for 2,293 lots of the day's total of 5,540, on the back of significant AA trades.
"There was a significant amount of Jan AAs which I think the roasters have given up papers...we should see the uncovered (positions) come down tomorrow," said one trader.
At the close of business on Friday, the uncovereds on the January contract stood at 8,420 lots.
New York arabica futures prices rallied sharply by about four U.S. cents from their intraday lows on a combination of local short covering and fresh commission house buying.
But London failed to rebound sharply, just managing to pull back by about $10 the most as the market ran into producer selling towards the highs.
The arbitrage between London and New York also widened slightly.
Earlier in the day, the market reacted negatively to upward crop revisions by the U.S. Department of Agriculture (USDA).
The USDA's world coffee estimate released after the market closed on Friday revised upward the 1996/97 crop for key robusta-growers Indonesia and Vietnam.
The USDA's semi-annual world crop forecast pegged global production for 1996/97 at 100.9 million 60-kg bags, up 1.8 million from the June forecast.

Broker GNI saw no real surprises in USDA figures but a reduction in Brazil's crop to 27 million bags from 27.5 million was a "bit of a slap in the face for the European traders" who had pegged the crop at 28-30 million bags.
Traders were keeping a close eye on Wednesday's expiry of December contract in New York. Analysts said the contract could be explosive unless the open interest dropped significantly.
Traders said London's certified coffee stocks rose to 2,104 five-tonne lots in November from 1,410 in October. The increase was in line with earlier market expectation.
